Pg. 40 of God's Church? "If God is with us" we may ex- claim with St. Paul, "who shall be against us?" My dear brethern; it is easy to know that God keeps His promises. It is easy to know that Jesus has been and is still with His Church. It is easy to know that His Church has triumphed & triumphed over error of every shape and color and form; that She has stood the test of 1900 years simply of existence but of a forward march till she stands Today a wonder even in the eyes of her persecutors. If St. Augustine could point to the Church of his time as a standing miracle of the 5th century, how much more manifestly is she not a standing miracle of the 20th century? It is easy to know too that not only Judas Iscariot and the pharisees and P. Pilot and the Grt. Ceasers did what they could - did the devil's worst against the Church even as against Himself, but that Judases & Pilots and ceasars have been never wanting to persecute to betray, to crucify the Church of Christ - the authority of the Living God -
Pg. 41 so much so that the history of the Church from the beginning has been the story repeated over and over again has been the story at once of the crucifiction and the Resurrection. Yet, dear Br: we are asked and urged to pray for the triumph of the Church of God. Why? Because the enemies of the Church, the enemies of God - of truth & justice are as determined today to crush religion as they were 1900 years ago.
Pg. 42 May 1, 1917 Behold the Handmade of the the Lord. Be it done ... word." Luke 1, 37 We must try this evening to join our May devotions with the devotion to the Sacred Heart. This, as every Catholic understands should not be difficult. It is related of Geo. Washington that though he was not a Catholic during his life, yet he always had a great veneration for the Blessed Virgin. On a cer- tain occasion a renowned educator from a Catholic country was visiting him and admiring a beautiful painting of the Madonna in his bedroom remarked, "why Mr. Washington, I did not know that you were a Catholic?" Washington's reply was simple, but earnes
